investments-in-2016.notes: Hint: use CTE, concat subquery for location, use exclusive logic using count and group

consecutive-numbers.notes: Hint: CTE full join using union

department-top-three-salaries.notes: Hint: CTE + inner join + dense_rank with partition to rank

tree-node.notes: Hint: use case and subquery to see if a node already exists as a p_id

exchange-seats.notes: Hint: use case and modulo to change the IDs, then reorder the IDs, don't forget about the last odd seat

customers-who-bought-all-products.notes: Hint: group by id, then use having and subquery counter

product-sales-analysis-iii.notes: Hint: subquery to store the true values of min when a tie occurs

product-price-at-a-given-date.notes: Hint: subquery to find the most recent pair of price and product ID, use union to make a default of 10 for unchanged prices before the date

market-analysis-i.notes: Hint: use left join to keep people with 0 orders; filters should be after the on clause for easy

last-person-to-fit-in-the-bus.notes: Hint: CTE to track the running total, use order by and limit in the main query to retrieve the last person

immediate-food-delivery-ii.notes: Hint: case to add to immediate orders, subquery to filter for first orders, don't use CTE

trips-and-users.notes: Hint: CTE and double inner join to filter banned users, case to sum cancels, and group by date

monthly-transactions-i.notes: Hint: use date_format to get rid of the day portion of the date; repeat when multigrouping

queries-quality-and-percentage.notes: Hint: pure math, don't forget to round

restaurant-growth.notes: Hint: use a CTE to count the number of customers in the given time frame and find the daily sum of all customers for every day, main query to find moving sum and moving average, use offset to remove days with invalid windows

count-salary-categories.notes: Hint: every row is an individual query; use union

list-the-products-ordered-in-a-period.notes: Hint: use date_format to get rid of the day from the date, and CTE to get the monthly total units per product_id

capital-gainloss.notes: Hint: group the stocks, then use if depending on the operation

movie-rating.notes: Hint: split the query into two and merge using union all, order by has two variables to consider and lexicographically smaller means name/title asc. [TC: O(R1 + R2log M), 2 passes]

confirmation-rate.notes: Hint: Use left join and group by carefully to include missing IDs not in Confirmations; otherwise, it's simple math. Also, use avg for one pass. [TC: O(S + C), 1 pass]

group-sold-products-by-the-date.notes: Hint: remember that only distinct pairs of (sell_date, product) are valid. Sort lexicographically using order by product asc in the group_concat. [TC: O(n), 1 pass]

patients-with-a-condition.notes: Hint: make sure that DIAB1 is either the beginning of the first condition name or the beginning of the condition name subsequently. [TC: O(n), 1 pass]

bank-account-summary-ii.notes: Hint: group by account number and filter using having and sum [TC: O(N+M), 1 pass]

percentage-of-users-attended-a-contest.notes: Hint: math problem, group by contest_id, then count, then divide by the total number of users. [TC: O(N+MlogM), 2 passes]

top-travellers.notes: Hint: users can exist without being on the rides table, so make sure null values default to 0; the same thing should be considered when joining. [TC: O(U+RlogU), 1 pass]

customer-who-visited-but-did-not-make-an.notes: Hint: join the two tables, then filter out the ones that have ID values in both tables. Group and sum the rest accordingly. [TC: O(V+T), 2 passes]

odd-and-even-transactions.notes: Hint: addition problem with modulo and case/if. [TC: O(N), 1 pass]

find-students-who-improved.notes: Hint: use a CTE to rank the rows by date of completion, partitioned for pairs of (student_id, subject) twice (chronologically and in reverse). Use a self-join in the main query on the same pairs of (student_id, subject) where firsts meet lasts and filter for improved scores. [TC: O(NlogN), 5 passes]

analyze-subscription-conversion.notes: Hint: almost pure logic/math question; make sure that the average part includes a distinct before the case statement to count only the distinct days the user has used the plan. Filter out the people who didn't upgrade from the free plan by only keeping those with activity durations in both the free and paid plans. [TC: O(NlogN), 4 passes]

find-users-with-valid-e-mails.notes: Hint: use regexp_like to get case sensitivity for the suffix, or use an extra like binary. Watch out for the period in the suffix, which is a wildcard, so put it in square brackets. [TC: O(N), 1 pass]
